claim: An error page on any of the six React Router apps renders with no nonce, so under the `strict-dynamic` policy those apps serve, its own client entry is blocked and the page never hydrates. The nonce reaches a page only through the root loader's data, which React Router does not give the render that wraps an ErrorBoundary. So the page a reader meets when something has already gone wrong is the one page that cannot report, recover or navigate, and it is reached precisely when those would be worth most.

evidence:
Every root route reads the nonce the same way. `alan/web/root.tsx:109`, `product/smilingjenny/web/root.tsx:28`, `product/audhdalan/web/root.tsx:30`, `alan/atlas-web/root.tsx:42`, `temper/web/root.tsx:72` and `product/archive-of-worlds/web/root.tsx:47` each hold `const nonce = useRouteLoaderData<typeof loader>("root")?.nonce`, and hand it to `<ScrollRestoration nonce={nonce} />` and `<Scripts nonce={nonce} />`. `security-headers.module.code.ts:31` writes `script-src 'self' 'nonce-...' 'strict-dynamic'`, under which a tag carrying no nonce does not run.

What the live sites answer, measured on 2026-09-13 after the exports were restored by `b218a5d9ab5` and each app was put up again. A page that resolves carries no un-nonced script: `https://audhdalan.com/` answers 200 with 0, `https://alanwalton.com/sign-in` answers 200 with 0, `https://smilingjenny.me/sign-in` answers 200 with 0, `https://archiveofworlds.app/sign-in` answers 200 with 0. A page that does not resolve carries three: `https://audhdalan.com/sign-in` answers 404 with 3, `https://smilingjenny.me/no-such-page` answers 404 with 3. The three are the two inline scripts React Router writes and the `<script type="module" async>` that imports the route modules, which is the client entry.

Why the two differ. On the error path React Router renders `Layout` around the `ErrorBoundary` without the root route's loader data, so `useRouteLoaderData("root")` answers `undefined` and every tag `Layout` writes loses its nonce. The loader itself is not at fault and did not throw: the same loader on the same deployment answers a resolving route with a nonce. The pod was read directly to rule out a stale build — `kubectl exec -n audhdalan deployment/web -c web -- grep -n loader /app/repo/product/audhdalan/web/root.tsx` answers `27:export const loader = rootNonceLoader`, which is the restored export.

What it costs. The error page's markup is server-rendered, so a reader sees the words. Nothing on it hydrates, so nothing on it is a route the client can leave by, and `ErrorCaptureInstaller` does not install, so an error page reports nothing about itself. The browser console on such a page carries the same pair of failures a wholly blocked page carries: the blocked-script notices, then `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'streamController')`, since the nonced streaming script reaches for a `window.__reactRouterContext` the blocked script never wrote.

The shape is the one `b218a5d9ab5` mended, in the one render path that mend does not reach. That landing restored seven route loaders the export sweep had stripped, which fixed every resolving page. It could not fix the error page, because there the nonce is absent for a reason that has nothing to do with the export.
